confirmed.title: SSH connect hangs forever (even after Cancel) when ssh exits while Ember decides, e.g. Cancel during the runtime download; the host stays 'connecting' until restart
confirmed.scenario: First connection to a new remote: after the probe, the decider downloads the runtime ('Downloading what Ember needs for build-01 (3 of 29 MB)…') and the user clicks Cancel. The same thing happens with the kill switch, Disconnect, or any network drop that ends ssh during the download. runAttempt's onAbort posts {t:'kill'} and the worker SIGKILLs ssh. Node destroys child.stdin when the child exits, so 'close' fires while nobody is listening. The aborted fetch then makes decide() answer QUIT, and runBootstrap calls writeAll(io.stdin, 'QUIT\n') at bootstrap.ts:565. Writing to an already-destroyed stream emits no 'error', no 'close' and no 'drain', so writeAll never settles. runBootstrap never resolves, reportExit is never called and no outcome or exit is posted. The worker's kill() returns early because `exited` is true (link-worker.ts:150-153), and runAttempt settles only on outcome, exit or worker exit. control.result therefore never resolves. Results: doConnect hangs; connections' `connecting` entry is never deleted, so every later connect() returns the same hung promise (connections.ts:680); the runtime's Conn stays 'connecting', so Connect and Reconnect answer {ok:true} and do nothing; the quit question says Ember is still connected to the host; the link worker thread is leaked. I reproduced this with runLinkCore + runAttempt in process (scratch hang2.ts): after Cancel, the attempt was still unsettled 5 s later, and in principle stays that way forever. A plain ssh exit during the download, without Cancel, also hung (hang.ts).
confirmed.fix: Make writeAll reject at once when `w.destroyed || w.writableEnded || (w as any).closed`, and keep an 'error' listener for the stream's whole life rather than only during write(). In runLinkCore, when ssh has exited during the bootstrap (onExit while state is 'starting'), post the outcome {kind:'eof'} and the exit (or make kill() on an exited child still finish the attempt), so runAttempt always settles. Also race runBootstrap's decide() against the reader's EOF.

The next writeAll then writes to a destroyed stream. I instrumented that write: `destroyed=true closed=true ret=false`. Writable._write only queues the callback for an already-destroyed stream; errorOrDestroy returns early, so no 'error', 'close' or 'drain' ever fires. writeAll at app/main/remote/bootstrap.ts:483 therefore waits on 'drain' forever.

**Both scenarios hang** (control.result was still unsettled after 8 s in each):
- Cancel: the child is SIGKILLed, then QUIT is written.
- Plain ssh exit (code 255) during a 1 s decide: then the INSTALL line is written.

**No guard elsewhere:**
- **Worker timers.** The worker's Deadline is cancelled at probe-begin and probeTimer is cleared in decide(). The "stuck" kill timer and reportExit are only set up in runBootstrap's .then, which never runs.
- **Worker kill() and exit.** kill() returns early once `exited` is true (link-worker.ts:150-153). onExit only acts in the ready or stalled states, so nothing posts the outcome or the exit.
- **runAttempt.** It settles only on outcome, exit or port exit. Its onAbort just posts kill.
- **connections.ts.** attempt() awaits control.result with no race. connect() hands back the hung `connecting` promise, and disconnect(), stopAll() and dispose() only call abort() without deleting the entry.

confirmed.title: cmd.run's PC timeout (5 s + idle RTT) is shorter than gate 2's own 5 s path inspection: the PC says 'wasn't started' while the remote starts the command, and nobody stops it
confirmed.scenario: The model runs `ls /mnt/nfs/data` (or anything whose operand or cwd is on a slow, stale or automounting NFS, autofs or sshfs path) on an SSH remote. The agent's run() awaits gateCommand, and its inspectSoon waits INSPECT_MS = 5000 ms before falling back (gate.ts:27,117). The PC's request timeout is OP_MS['cmd.run'] = 5000 ms plus the link's minimum RTT (remote-sidecar.ts:100,106-108), and it starts before the request even leaves the PC. The PC therefore always gives up first. The WorkerLink deletes the pending id, and RemoteRun.notStarted ends the run 'failed-to-start: build-01 didn't answer in time, so the command wasn't started'. That is what the model and the command window's tab are told. Milliseconds later the gate answers ok and the agent writes its audit entry and starts the run (serve.ts:389-421). The 'started' answer is dropped because no request is pending, so no cmd.stop is ever sent. The command runs on the remote with no tab and no Stop button, and the task's Stop can't reach it; only the kill switch, its own timeout (up to 900 s) or a disconnect does. The model, told it didn't start, is likely to run it again, so it runs twice. Reproduced with the real WorkerLink, createRemoteRunner and gateCommand plus a hanging inspect (scratch cmdrun-race.ts): at 5.012 s the PC ended the run as failed-to-start, at 5.014 s the agent's gate said ok and the run started, and the only request the PC ever sent was cmd.run.
confirmed.fix: Give cmd.run a PC-side limit well above the agent's worst case before starting (INSPECT_MS + facts + classify, e.g. 15 s + RTT), or cap the agent's gate below the PC's limit. In either case, when cmd.run times out, send cmd.stop {runId, why:'task'} (whileStalled), so a run the agent starts late is ended.

confirmed.title: A remote command's output is queued in the agent's memory without limit; after a fast printer, the link's bulk lane stays clogged for minutes (Stop included)
confirmed.scenario: RemoteRuns forwards every stdout and stderr 'data' chunk straight to mux.sendBytes (commands.ts:160-166; main.ts:187). It never pauses the child. The mux queues bulk bytes without bound: credit limits only what is on the wire (mux.ts:441). MX's hand-off told SB to cap the backlog with backlog(), but nothing calls it (grep finds no use). Running `cat` on a multi-GB log, `journalctl`, `find /`, or a verbose build on a remote over a 1 MB/s link: in my scratch run (mux-backlog.ts: real createMux on both ends, a 1 MB/s link and a real RemoteRuns) a 300 MB output was 241.6 MB queued in the agent after 1 s, and RSS went from about 170 to 418 MB. A multi-GB output grows the agent's memory until the remote OOMs or the watchdog trips. The bulk queue is FIFO across channels (mux.ts:612), and neither Stop, the kill switch nor the run's end drops a channel's queued bytes. So after the run ends or is stopped, the backlog keeps draining at link speed for minutes. On the PC each later command's bytes arrive only after it. RemoteRun waits just TAIL_MS (2 s) after cmd.exit and then ends with whatever arrived, so the model silently gets truncated or empty output. Screenshots (also bulk) time out, so the remote is effectively unusable until the backlog drains.
confirmed.fix: Pause the run's stdout and stderr while the mux's bulk backlog is above a cap (for example 1-4 MiB), and resume when it drains. Drop or stop queuing a run's channel once the PC stops listening or the run is stopped. Alternatively, keep only a bounded head and tail per run on the agent, and report the omitted bytes in cmd.exit.

confirmed.title: Remote desktop helper (and its on-screen notice) is started after Stop when a desktop.state was in flight
confirmed.scenario: The PC asks for desktop.state before every task (targets/runtime.ts handsFor calls desktopNow). ensureNow awaits discover(true), which runs loginctl and busctl, then calls this.stop() and startChild(f, ask) with no check that a stop came meanwhile. If the user presses the PC's kill switch (the 'stop' op calls killSwitch, which calls desktop.stop()) or the remote person presses Stop on the notice (consoleStop) while that discovery is running, then once discovery returns the agent spawns a new desktop child, which shows 'Ember is using this screen' again and keeps its sidecar running until the next stop or disconnect. A policy change that turns ssh.desktop off during the same window is bypassed in the same way, because `ask.allowed` was computed before the await. Reproduced with DesktopController (scratch desk-race.ts): ensure(), then stop() 100 ms later, while discovery takes 300 ms. Output: 'stop() called; child pid now: null', then 'desktop child spawned (after stop: true)'.
confirmed.fix: Give DesktopController a generation counter that stop() increments. ensureNow captures it before discover() and returns {access:'none'} without spawning if it changed. Re-read `allowed` from the server after the await, and drop the cached `starting` promise on stop().
